items.name: Kubernetes RCA (kaop)
items.description: Disconnected, in-cluster root-cause analysis for Kubernetes workloads. Investigates a single resource using read-only kubectl against the local cluster — no Komodor backend, no external data sources. Built from Klaudia's RCA knowledge (investigation methodology, change-timeline reconstruction, domain expertise). Deployed in Kubernetes cluster 'kaop' and can only investigate resources in that cluster — route an RCA for a resource in 'kaop' to this agent.

items.name: Base Evaluator
items.description: Komodor's base LLM-as-judge, deployable from the worker catalog. Grades a standalone run against an eval rule's rubric and instructions and returns one 0..1 score per requested rubric, each with its own rationale; and blindly compares a dual-deploy shadow pair's two runs against each other, scoring each on every criterion and summarizing what separates them. Which of the two it does is decided by how many runs the grade task carries: one for a standalone grade, two (blinded "run_a"/"run_b") for a comparison. It returns the verdict as the run output, which the control plane records as a score on the graded run(s).

{"run_id":"run_5c3ba4caa44fa229b5c43a19","status":"succeeded","output":{"text":"**Root cause:** The `orders-fastpath` canary deployment, created at 23:27:48Z, runs pods labelled `app=orders`. That matches the `orders` Service selector, so its pod joined the Service endpoints. It is hard-coded to return HTTP 500, and kube-proxy sends about 1 in 3 checkout requests to it.

**Why only some checkouts fail:** The `orders` Service has three endpoints. Two are healthy `orders` pods; one is the canary, which always returns 500. Traffic spreads roughly evenly, so about a third of checkouts fail. Measured: 31 of 180 recent shopper requests returned 500, all starting after the canary appeared. Counting only requests made after 23:27:48, the rate is close to 1/3.

## Evidence
- **The canary's labels match the Service.** `deploy/orders-fastpath` pod template labels are `{app: orders, track: fastpath}`. `svc/orders` selects on `app=orders` only.
- **The canary pod is in the Service endpoints.** `endpoints/orders` = `10.244.0.139:8080, 10.244.0.140:8080, 10.244.0.145:8080`. The last one, `.145`, is `orders-fastpath-8476ddbc8b-hn9hb`.
- **The canary always returns 500.** Its container args are `["-listen=:8080","-text=order accepted","-status-code=500"]`. The healthy `orders` pods have no `-status-code` argument, so they return 200.
- **Its own annotation says it should not get traffic.** `description: "Canary of the new orders fast path. Not wired into the storefront yet."` and `owner: payments-team`. Leaving out a Service selector is not enough to keep it off the Service, because the label overlap puts it there anyway.
- **Canary logs show storefront traffic reaching it:**
  `2026/10/21 23:30:37 orders:8080 10.244.0.146:53010 "GET /checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 15 "curl/8.23.0"`
  The source IPs `.146` and `.147` are the storefront pods.
- **Storefront logs show the 500s passing through:**
  `10.244.0.143 - - [21/Oct/2026:23:28:53 +0000] "GET /checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 15`
  - djgp6: 9 of 36 checkouts returned 500.
  - nzl9l: 8 of 23 checkouts returned 500.
- **Shopper (synthetic client) logs:** only 200s from 23:24:49. The first 500 is at `23:27:52`, 4 seconds after the canary was created. The single `000` at 23:24:47 was a startup race and is unrelated.
- **Storefront config is fine.** ConfigMap `storefront` routes `location /` to `proxy_pass http://orders:8080;`, which is correct. The ConfigMap has not changed since it was created at 23:24:46Z.

## Timeline (UTC, 2026-10-21)
| Time | Change |
|---|---|
| 23:24:46–47 | `orders` (rev 1), `storefront` (rev 1), `shopper`, `newsletter` and ConfigMap `storefront` created. Checkouts return 200. |
| **23:27:48** | **`orders-fastpath` created (RS `8476ddbc8b`). Its pod `.145` joins `endpoints/orders`.** |
| 23:27:52 | First checkout 500. |
| 23:28:48 | `storefront` restarted (`kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt: 2026-10-22T01:28:48+02:00`, giving rev 2). The template is otherwise unchanged. 500s continue, so the restart was a symptom response and did not fix anything. |

## Fix
Take the canary pod out of the `orders` Service. Either option works:
1. **Preferred:** in `deploy/orders-fastpath`, change the label in both `spec.selector.matchLabels` and `spec.template.metadata.labels` from `app: orders` to something like `app: orders-fastpath`. The selector field can't be changed in place, so the Deployment has to be deleted and re-created.
2. **Immediate mitigation:** scale `deploy/orders-fastpath` to `replicas: 0`. Alternatively, change `svc/orders` `spec.selector` to `{app: orders, track: stable}` and add `track: stable` to the `orders` pod template.

Once the fix is in, check that `kubectl get endpoints orders -n shop` lists only `.139` and `.140`, and that the shopper logs go back to all 200s. The canary itself also needs to stop returning 500 (remove `-status-code=500`) before it gets real traffic.

## Checked and not the cause
- **`newsletter` is in CrashLoopBackOff (6 restarts), but it is unrelated.** Its script always ends in `exit 1` after trying `mail.internal:25`. It has no Service and is not in the checkout path. Its logs could not be read (`unable to retrieve container logs`). It still needs a separate fix.
- There are no NetworkPolicies, HPAs or PDBs in `shop`. No Secrets are referenced by any workload.
- Every pod except newsletter is Running/Ready with 0 restarts.

## Confidence and limits
**Confidence: high.** The start of the failures lines up to the second with the canary's creation, and its logs show it answering storefront's checkout calls with 500.

What the cluster can't show:
- who applied `orders-fastpath`; the annotation names `payments-team` as owner but not the person
- who ran the storefront restart
- anything before 23:24:46, when the namespace's resources were first created"},"error":null,"session_id":"5bb1b7ed-f73c-4f12-b27f-d2d0f6462aba"}

content.content:
{"run_id":"run_b43d000fadafee99ba6779b5","status":"succeeded","output":{"text":"I scaled `orders-fastpath` in `shop` to 0 replicas, and the 500s stopped: all 33 checkouts after the change returned 200. Nothing else was changed, and the deployment still exists.

**What failed:** about 1 in 5 checkouts returned HTTP 500 (50 of 251 in the window before the fix).

**Root cause:** `orders-fastpath` is payments-team's canary. Its pod has the label `app=orders`, which matches the `orders` Service selector, so it was taking a share of the traffic. It runs with `-status-code=500`, so every request it got failed. Its own description says "Not wired into the storefront yet", but the storefront sends `/checkout` to `orders:8080` (I checked its ConfigMap), so the canary was in the live path.

**Timeline (UTC, 2026-10-21):**
- About 23:27:30: `orders-fastpath` was created (age 3m41s at my first check) and was added to `endpoints/orders`.
- 23:33:02: last 500 seen by the shopper.
- 23:33:11: scale applied.
- 23:33:12 onward: only 200s.

## Commands and output

**1. State before the fix**
```
$ kubectl -n shop get endpoints orders
orders   10.244.0.139:8080,10.244.0.140:8080,10.244.0.145:8080
$ kubectl -n shop get deploy orders-fastpath -o jsonpath='{...args}'
["-listen=:8080","-text=order accepted","-status-code=500"]
```
`10.244.0.145` is the fastpath pod. Its annotations include `owner: payments-team`.

**2. The fix**
```
$ date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ; kubectl -n shop scale deployment/orders-fastpath --replicas=0
2026-10-21T23:33:11Z
deployment.apps/orders-fastpath scaled
```

**3. Check (1): the fastpath pod is gone; check (2): endpoints list only the healthy pods**
```
$ kubectl -n shop get deploy orders-fastpath
orders-fastpath   0/0     0            0           5m35s
$ kubectl -n shop get pods -l app=orders -o wide
orders-574f6fc5b9-c4fst   1/1   Running   10.244.0.139
orders-574f6fc5b9-v26wd   1/1   Running   10.244.0.140
$ kubectl -n shop get endpoints orders
orders   10.244.0.139:8080,10.244.0.140:8080
$ kubectl -n shop get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=orders
orders-dmrjh   IPv4   8080   10.244.0.140,10.244.0.139
```
Both match what you expected.

**4. Check (3): checkout results**

These come from the shopper pod, which calls `curl http://storefront/checkout` about every 2 seconds:
```
$ kubectl -n shop logs deploy/shopper --since-time=2026-10-21T23:33:12Z --timestamps
2026-10-21T23:33:12.80Z 23:33:12 200
... (one line about every 2s, all 200) ...
2026-10-21T23:34:17.20Z 23:34:17 200
--- counts:
     33 200
```

| Window (UTC) | 200 | 500 | other |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before: 23:24:47 – 23:33:10 | 200 | 50 | 1 × `000` |
| **After: 23:33:12 – 23:34:17** | **33** | **0** | 0 |

The "before" window also covers about 3 minutes before the canary existed, so its 500 rate understates how bad it was once the canary was live. The single `000` (no response) was most likely during the storefront rollout at about 23:28:50; it's unrelated.

## Notes
- **No direct pod checks:** my service account isn't allowed to run commands inside pods (`kubectl exec` / `pods/exec` was refused). So I couldn't curl each pod individually, and the request counts come from the shopper's existing traffic instead.

# Incident Report: Intermittent checkout failures in the `shop` namespace

**Date:** 2026-10-21 (UTC)
**Status:** Mitigated and verified
**Tools used:** KAOP agents *Kubernetes RCA (kaop)* (read-only investigation) and *Shop Remediator* (applied the fix and verified it)

## 1. What failed

Some `GET /checkout` requests through the `storefront` returned **HTTP 500**. The rest succeeded.
- Measured by the RCA agent: 31 of 180 recent shopper requests returned 500. All of them came after the canary appeared, and the post-canary failure rate was about 1/3.
- Measured by the remediator over the whole window before the fix (23:24:47–23:33:10): 200 × 200, 50 × 500, 1 × 000. The 500 share looks lower here because this window includes about 3 minutes before the canary existed.

## 2. Root cause

Deployment `orders-fastpath` is a canary owned by `payments-team`. Its pod template carries the labels `app: orders, track: fastpath`. The `orders` Service selects only on `app=orders`, so the canary pod was added to the Service's endpoints next to the two healthy `orders` pods.

The canary container runs with `-status-code=500`, so it fails **every** request it gets. kube-proxy spreads traffic across all three endpoints, so roughly **1 in 3 checkouts** reached the canary and failed. That is why only some checkouts failed.

The canary's own annotation says *"Canary of the new orders fast path. Not wired into the storefront yet."* Not giving it its own Service did not keep it out of the path, because its labels overlap with the `orders` Service selector.

## 3. Evidence

- **Label overlap:** `deploy/orders-fastpath` has template labels `{app: orders, track: fastpath}`. `svc/orders` has selector `{app: orders}`.
- **Canary pod in the endpoints:** `endpoints/orders` = `10.244.0.139:8080, 10.244.0.140:8080, 10.244.0.145:8080`. `.145` is `orders-fastpath-8476ddbc8b-hn9hb`.
- **Canary is set to fail:** its args are `["-listen=:8080","-text=order accepted","-status-code=500"]`. The healthy `orders` pods have no `-status-code` argument.
- **Canary logs show storefront traffic reaching it:**
  `2026/10/21 23:30:37 orders:8080 10.244.0.146:53010 "GET /checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 15 "curl/8.23.0"`
  The sources `10.244.0.146` and `.147` are the storefront pods.
- **Storefront logs show the 500s passing through:** `"GET /checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 15`. Pod djgp6 had 9 of 36 checkouts fail; pod nzl9l had 8 of 23.
- **Timing:** the first 500 in the shopper logs is at 23:27:52, 4 seconds after `orders-fastpath` was created at 23:27:48.
- **Storefront config is not the cause:** ConfigMap `storefront` has `proxy_pass http://orders:8080;`, which is correct, and it has not changed since it was created.

## 4. Timeline (UTC, 2026-10-21)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 23:24:46–47 | `orders`, `storefront`, `shopper`, `newsletter` and ConfigMap `storefront` created. Checkouts return 200. |
| **23:27:48** | **`orders-fastpath` canary created. Its pod (10.244.0.145) joins `endpoints/orders`.** |
| 23:27:52 | First checkout 500. |
| 23:28:48 | `storefront` restarted (rollout restart, rev 2, template otherwise unchanged). 500s continue, so the restart did not help. |
| 23:33:02 | Last 500 seen. |
| **23:33:11** | **Fix applied: `orders-fastpath` scaled to 0.** |
| 23:33:12 onward | Only 200s. |

## 5. Fix applied

```
kubectl -n shop scale deployment/orders-fastpath --replicas=0
```

This takes the faulty canary pod out of the `orders` Service. It is the smallest change that stops the failures and is easy to undo. The Deployment was **not** deleted (it belongs to payments-team), and nothing else was changed.

### Recommended permanent fix (payments-team)

Before the canary is scaled back up:
1. Give it labels the `orders` Service does not match, in **both** `spec.selector.matchLabels` and `spec.template.metadata.labels`. For example, use `app: orders-fastpath`. The selector field is immutable, so the Deployment has to be deleted and re-created. Another option is to make the Service selector stricter: `{app: orders, track: stable}`, with `track: stable` added to the `orders` pods.
2. Remove `-status-code=500` before the canary takes real traffic.

**Warning:** running `kubectl -n shop scale deployment/orders-fastpath --replicas=1` without step 1 will bring the failures back.

## 6. Verification

- `kubectl -n shop get deploy orders-fastpath` returns `0/0`, and no fastpath pod is running.
- `kubectl -n shop get endpoints orders` returns `10.244.0.139:8080,10.244.0.140:8080`, which are the two healthy `orders` pods only. The EndpointSlice matches.
- Checkout traffic: `kubectl -n shop logs deploy/shopper --since-time=2026-10-21T23:33:12Z` shows the shopper calling `storefront/checkout` about every 2 seconds:

| Window (UTC) | 200 | 500 | other |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before fix: 23:24:47–23:33:10 | 200 | 50 | 1 × 000 (startup race, unrelated) |
| **After fix: 23:33:12–23:34:17** | **33** | **0** | 0 |

**Limitation:** the remediator's service account cannot use `pods/exec`, so it did not curl individual pods. The check relies on the shopper's real ongoing checkout traffic.

## 7. Other findings (not related to checkouts)

- `newsletter` is in CrashLoopBackOff. Its script tries `mail.internal:25` and always ends with `exit 1`. It has no Service and is not in the checkout path. It needs its own fix and was left untouched.
- There are no NetworkPolicies, HPAs or PDBs in `shop`, and no workload references a Secret.
- The cluster records cannot tell who applied `orders-fastpath` or who restarted `storefront`.

content.text:
I've fixed the checkout failures in `shop` and written the full analysis to `report.md`. Checkouts are working again: 33 out of 33 succeeded after the fix, compared with 50 failures before it.

**What failed:** about 1 in 3 checkouts got an HTTP 500 error after 23:27:52 UTC. The two healthy `orders` pods kept answering normally.

**Root cause:** at 23:27:48 the payments team created a test version of the orders service, the `orders-fastpath` deployment.
